extracted.intended_audience: business journalists, newsroom editors, SABEW members, and readers of journalism awards news
extracted.subtask_short: SABEW Best in Business awards announcement
extracted.subtask_description: An announcement of the 31st annual SABEW Best in Business Awards listing winners and summarizing what the competition honors. The page highlights award categories, top-winning outlets, and qualities praised by judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of excellence in business journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: SABEW launched the Best in Business competition in 1995 to recognize excellence in the industry; the awards honor excellence in business journalism from 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General framing for the contest — entries are judged with the goal of identifying excellent business journalism across outlets and categories. No detailed scoring rubric is given on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Range of Work Award — breadth across platforms and categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual journalists were recognized for their exceptional coverage in SABEW’s Best Range of Work Award, where their submissions crossed a broad spectrum of content platforms and categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners cited (Hannah Natanson, Jessica Fu, Dustin Walsh) illustrate that judges value submissions demonstrating range across multiple platforms and topic categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stellar, insightful, and impactful content
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest is described as showcasing 'stellar, insightful and impactful content' from a wide range of publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges and organizers emphasize journalism that is not just well-crafted but offers insight and real-world impact; this language signals those qualities as evaluative priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting that exposes harmful business arrangements or decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges noted winners 'revealed unsavory business arrangements and investment decisions that harmed communities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative or explanatory work that uncovers harmful practices and holds business actors accountable is presented as a valued dimension of award-worthy coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear explanation of the uneven impact of major government and corporate policy decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners 'plainly explained the uneven impact of major government and corporate policy decisions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity in explaining complex policy and corporate effects on different communities is highlighted as a criterion for strong entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoming reporting roadblocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges observed that many winners 'often [overcame] roadblocks to their coverage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persistence, creative reporting methods, and overcoming obstacles to obtain substantive reporting are noted as characteristics of award-winning work.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Excellence (newsroom-level evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: General Excellence award winners were named by newsroom size: The New York Times (large), CNBC (medium), and STAT (small).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates a newsroom-wide assessment of overall quality across output and categories; evaluation appears stratified by newsroom size but specific scoring criteria are not detailed on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Media Outlet award
rubrics_metrics.description: Student reporters at the Howard Centers for Investigative Journalism at the University of Maryland and Arizona State University won the Student Media Outlet award for 'Off the Rails.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a dedicated recognition for student-produced work, implying different category eligibility but the page does not list explicit judging standards for student entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-based recognition (stories for professional news organizations and other categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners are named across many categories (e.g., Stories for Professional News Organizations); Quinn Waller won in that category for a specific story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contest is organized into multiple categories, each producing winners; while categories are mentioned, this page does not provide the specific judging criteria for each category — only that entries are evaluated within category frameworks.
